name: Answer explicitly names the NPE/crash consequence vs merely recommends a null guard without naming any exception
side_a: Do not deduct when the answer explicitly names the exception or crash that results from the null dereference (e.g., 'will throw a NullPointerException', 'NPE', 'crashing your application'), even if the recommendation itself is hedged, conditional, or phrased as 'you don't necessarily need to'.
side_b: Deduct 1 point when the answer only advises adding a null guard / null-safe idiom (e.g., 'if mPrefix can ever be null you should guard against it', 'use StringUtils.isNotEmpty') and never names NullPointerException or any thrown-exception/crash consequence — recommending defensive coding is not discussing the possible NPE.
